text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE GLOBE AND MAIL: Prenatal HIV testing urged: New estimate of babies at risk prompts Ontario doctor to recommend routine checks
-Swiss bank list prompts questions: Includes names of Nazis, non-Jews
-U.K. set for big political shakeup: Scots to get vote on own parliament
-Canadian businessman rules Moscow bar scene: Doug Steele packs them into the Hungry Duck with offers of free beer and tequila giveaways.
-Megacity law survives court challenge: Act not unconstitutional, judge rules
-Pension funds flee Altamira: Poor performance, drawn-out ownership battle sinking former star of mutual fund industry
-Michigan strike hits GM Canada: Auto maker tells 3,000 workers at Southern Ontario car plants to stay at home for want of transmissions
-CRTC abandons cultural red flag: Won't delist U.S. channels to make way for Canadian rivals
-Firms dig in for battle over Venezuelan gold: Placer Dome and Crystallex each claim to own the Las Crisinas mine. Observers can only guess who is right.
Mergers loom in oilpatch: Missed production targest are set to force share prices lower and put harder hit smaller firms in the takeover line of fire
-Bankers Trust called in to sort out Semi-Tech
